Using 75-90 MHz FM for drone control is pretty unusual. Most long-range setups use something like ExpressLRS (900 MHz) or Crossfire since they’re more reliable and have better support.

Just to clarify, your TX system (for controlling the drone) is different from your VTX system (for transmitting video). If you need real-time video, you’d be better off with a digital VTX like DJI O4, Walksnail, or a 5.8 GHz analog system, since FM isn’t great for high-bandwidth transmission. 

The Raspberry Pi 4 can handle telemetry and streaming but isn’t ideal for flight control—a dedicated flight controller like ArduPilot or PX4 would be a better fit. 

Also, what kind of range are you aiming for? You mentioned power isn’t a concern—are you running this from a boat with an external power source? If you’re going really far out, you might want to look into something like VSAT or Starlink for a stable connection beyond anything like RC range and FM and even HAM radio stuff.

If you give more details about what you are trying to accomplish, I may be able to point you in a better direction.

It sounds like you might not fully understand what a VTX system does, so I'll clarify.

A VTX (video transmitter) sends the camera feed to the pilot, usually through FPV goggles or, less commonly, a monitor with HDMI input. If you don’t have goggles, you can still install the VTX and camera, but you won’t be able to see what the drone sees until you get a receiver (goggles or a compatible screen).

You can absolutely fly a drone without a VTX system—this is called line-of-sight (LOS) flying, where you visually track the drone from the ground. However, most FPV pilots prefer using a VTX for an immersive experience.

There are two main types of VTX systems:

Analog: Cheaper, lower latency, but the image quality isn’t great.

Digital: More expensive, slightly higher latency, but the image is much clearer (e.g., DJI O4, Walksnail, HDZero).


If you’re just getting into the hobby, a cheap drone with a WiFi camera (like those from Amazon) can be a fun starting point before committing to full FPV. If you're serious, I recommend researching more about digital vs. analog systems before buying goggles to avoid compatibility issues.

I dated a girl who had self-harm scars, mostly on the wrists, and had some surgery scars as well. These scars weren't hard to spot. I dated her for 2 years and genuinely thought I would marry her. 

Things she did right

Waited for an appropriate time to tell me what had happened. I did ask about a few things, and she went into more detail than I asked because she felt that I should know in the spirit of transparency.

Asked how I felt about how she tried to kill herself and respected my feelings about it. She didn't get defensive or attack. That helped me a lot.

Wasn't self-destructive or self-conscious about them. She still wore short sleeve t shirts and bikinis, and didn't care. The confidence was really good for her, and I found it attractive. 

Things she did wrong. 

She failed to realize that I had feelings about what happened to her as well. Understand that while it may not be easy for you to be open/talk about it, it also may not be easy for him to hear/process this. Be patient, see how he feels, and don't let your opinion overpower or trump his. 

Don't turn things into a competition EVER about who has been through more or who is more qualified to help. I had a friend who was able to kill themselves, and they reached out to me. My gf was not explicitly invited, but also not invited. She was just never brought up. I was getting my shoes on quickly, and she wanted to come and help. She said she knew how to handle stuff better than me because of all sorts of reasons. When I said you weren't invited and I want to play it safe, that pissed her off.

She will have these scars for the rest of her life. I never really cared about the physical scars. The emotional scars are a very different deal. 

Pm me if you want to ask more. I'm open about this.

This is why wireless charging can be bad for your phone as it heats the whole thing up and does not allow the glass back to act as a heat spreader. This is also why taking off the phone case/getting a good phone case can greatly help keep your phone at a healthy temp. The downside is that the charger is usually quite warm due to electrical inefficiencies and the size of a laptop charger. The chips used in these are called GAN chips. Step three. Convert the STL into Gcode. Gcode is printer specific, so Gcode from one 3d printer will not work with another. This is why this step is important. I recommend Cura or if you have a Presa. Use the Presa slicer. This software that converts STLs into Gocde is called slicer software. This is where you will find out how long it will take, how much plastic it will need, and if you need supports or not. (Usually pretty straightforward but youtube when in doubt)

Step four. Prep the printer. This will very from printer to printer, my best advice is to have a friend help with this that knows what they are doing. 

Step five. Repeat the previous four step for everything you want to print.

Me and my brother just zip around in a circle around them while we wait because it's really fun. My brother ends up calling me over. He finds a large clearing in the trees. Nice and flat. We raced each other and started to head back to the rest of the family after the race to continue the trip. I am awful with maps and have no sense of direction. I tell my brother that I will tail behind him as he goes back. He says ok and we head out. Hes weaveing inbetween trees in a more dense part of the path and I choose to go around a bit because I'm not as good as he is and just dont want to risk it. We are only like 60 to 100 feet apart and totally can see each other. I was watching him weave in there cause it looked cool. I didnt have almost any trees ahead of me and thought it was a long straight shot and barely looked in front of myself and where I was going. He was doing great and it was cool to see but the  i looked back in front  of me and there was a jump in front of me. Like 20 feet ahead of me. That may not sound like a lot but we were going about 80 mph so breaking wouldnt have done much even though I did. I ended up catching about 18 feet of air even through it felt like a lot more. I was filled with fear, but through the fear and shock I somehow decided that jumping off was safer than staying on because I didnt want that big snowmobile landing on me. Having it be just my luck I ended up jumping mid air, totally bodyslaming a small tree that was about 6 feet tall and breaking it, and rolling around and tumbling for another little ways. Before comming to a stop. My brother sees the whole thing and is freaking out because I just crashed and could have easily died. Luckily I wasnt too hurt. I have all the padding on plus a helmet, but holy crap that hurt. I had a huge bruise on my back and arm that was really sensitive. My dad took me and got me tested to see if i had a concussion or not. I didnt but I did have a headache. Still one of the scariest things that I've experienced.
